🔻 Iran voices against nuclear monopoly, calls for equal access to advanced technologies

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Hossein Derakhshandeh, the deputy head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) has outlined four key priorities for equitable development of nuclear power globally, without any monopoly on the related technology.

Derakhshandeh, who is also CEO of the Nuclear Power Production and Development Company of Iran, made the proposal at the 'International Ministerial Conference on Nuclear Power,' hosted by South Korea on Tuesday.
​
Emphasizing the need to remove discriminatory barriers, facilitate access to advanced technologies, expand technical cooperation, and strengthen international measures for the protection of peaceful nuclear facilities, he stated that these technologies must not be turned into a tool for creating monopolies.
​
The AEOI deputy chief also called for equal access to advanced nuclear technologies, in accordance with the principles of international law and free from any double standards, saying Iran reaffirms the inalienable right of states party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) to conduct research, development, and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
​
Stressing the need to respect the rights of NPT signatories, he urged the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to act as an independent, technical, and development-oriented body, under the Statute that tasks it with promoting the peaceful use of nuclear energy and fostering technical cooperation among member states, without discrimination.
​
Regrettably, however, experience in recent years has shown that the IAEA has become subject to political considerations, straying from the impartial execution of its statutory responsibilities, he noted, citing unlawful US-Israeli attacks on Iran's peaceful nuclear facilities.
​
These American and Israeli attacks constitute a blatant violation of the United Nations Charter, international law, and the resolutions of the IAEA General Conference prohibiting attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities, Derakhshandeh said, accusing the Agency of failing to effectively uphold the fundamental principles of impartiality and professionalism.
​
Insisting that the protection of peaceful nuclear infrastructure is a shared international obligation, he denounced the silence on the violation of the rights of the Iranian nation across various sectors, including energy, healthcare, food security, the environment, and industry.
​
Regrettably, the Israeli regime, the United States, and certain European countries—driven by political agendas—persistently engage in smear campaigns, leveling baseless accusations and orchestrating negative media narratives, he added.

KEYSTONE TO DESTROY 18,835 HARDWARE WALLETS AFTER HACKERS STEAL DEVICE AUTHENTICATION KEY

Keystone has confirmed it will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets in existing inventory after attackers stole the cryptographic key used to verify the authenticity of its devices.

The breach is particularly concerning because the stolen key could allow attackers to manufacture counterfeit Keystone wallets that successfully pass the company's official authenticity checks, potentially putting users' Bitcoin at risk.

The key is permanently embedded in existing devices and cannot be erased or replaced, forcing Keystone to destroy its remaining inventory, suspend shipments and manufacture new devices with a replacement key.

⚡️ Iraq opposes politicization of pilgrimage affairs: Ambassador

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iraq’s ambassador to Iran has said that the Iraqi government insists that pilgrimage affairs between the two neighboring countries must not be politicized or face any interruption.

Yasser Abdul-Zahra Al-Hajjaj made the remarks in a meeting with Seyed Abdolfattah Navvab, the Representative of the Supreme Leader in Hajj and Pilgrimage Affairs, where he stressed that Iraq is fully prepared to resolve the issues surrounding the land and air travel of Iranian pilgrims to Iraq.
​
During the meeting, Seyed Abdolfattah Navvab referred to the martyred Leader’s appreciation for the generosity and hospitality of the Iraqi people, conveying his gratitude to the Iraqi nation.
​
The Iranian side also stressed the urgent need to launch the railway route between the two countries to facilitate the growing number of pilgrims from both countries. He also emphasized the necessity of further developing Iraq’s pilgrimage cities to enhance the welfare of pilgrims.

📡 Leader of Islamic Revolution meets with Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, has met with Major General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

During the meeting, Ayatollah Khamenei described the Supreme National Security Council and its Secretariat as the “crossroads of policymaking” in the country’s affairs.
​
He emphasized the interconnectedness of four areas—culture, politics, the economy, and security—and the need for decisions in each area to be accompanied by appropriate supporting measures.
​
The Leader of the Islamic Revolution stressed that sound and well-grounded decisions require a roadmap based on a comprehensive understanding of each undertaking, from its starting point to its conclusion.
​
Other key topics discussed during the meeting included strengthening national cohesion and unity, as well as mutual trust between the people and officials; making use of the capacities provided by the Constitution, particularly Article 176, to assist the President and executive bodies in facilitating and expediting the resolution of the country's problems; safeguarding national and regional security by maintaining control over the Strait of Hormuz; and strengthening bilateral relations with neighboring countries on the basis of lasting and mutual interests.
​
The Leader of the Islamic Revolution described the enemy's desperation as one of the fruits of national resistance. He also emphasized the need for proactive and timely communication in order to sustain the people's continued participation in defending the country and the system. He further stressed the need to pursue the rights and interests of the Iranian nation and the Resistance Front by ensuring that the conditions set forth by the country’s officials for ending the war are met and by bringing the current state of “neither war nor peace” to an end.
​
During the meeting, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council presented a report on the country's situation across various sectors and ongoing efforts. In his report, Dr. Mohsen Rezaei identified the pursuit of the Islamic Republic's strategic policy of “establishing endogenous regional arrangements and order” as one of the initiatives currently being undertaken by the Secretariat of the Supreme National Security Council.
